paper_id: FreeEagle_ Detecting Complex Neural Trojans in Data-Free Cases
title: FreeEagle: Detecting Complex Neural Trojans in Data-Free Cases
motivation: Model-sharing platforms need to detect trojaned models, but lack access to clean validation data or samples with triggers.
problem_framing: Data-free detection of complex backdoors including class-specific attacks and evasive triggers without any auxiliary data.
key_insight: Trojaned classifier assigns trigger features higher priority than benign features; generating dummy IRs reveals this priority shift.
method_signature: Generate dummy intermediate representations at classifier input via gradient descent; detect posterior outliers.
evaluation_criteria: Detection effectiveness across diverse datasets, model architectures, trigger types, and attack strategies.
negative_result_or_admitted_limitation: DF-TND is ineffective against class-specific backdoors and evasive triggers, and does not generalize to small models.
evidence_for_taste: focus on analyzing the behavior of the classifier part
generating dummy intermediate representations rather than dummy raw inputs
inspecting the classifier part rather than the entire model significantly reduces the time cost
inspired by the classic anomaly detection method box plot
thinking_moves: 把数据缺失问题转化为优化生成dummy样本问题
聚焦于模型分类器部分而非整体以降低搜索空间
从统计异常检测(box plot)角度设计异常度量指标
预判可能自适应攻击而设置分离层位置策略
利用生成dummy中间表示规避真实数据依赖
